records.notes: Writer/scribe or adjectival active participle; also Form III perfect كَاتَبَ and imperative كَاتِبْ. No clitic boundary.
Passive participle written; also a written document/letter or that which is prescribed, used substantivally.
School مَدْرَسَة, or feminine teacher/teaching/taught مُدَرِّسَة/مُدَرَّسَة. The school suffix can be lexical or derivational; the participial feminine ending is inflectional.
Key or means of opening; instrument noun. The internal م and ا belong to the derived stem.
Form X verbal noun seeking forgiveness; the derivational prefix and internal vowels remain in the stem.
Form X active/passive participle مُسْتَخْرِج/مُسْتَخْرَج, or an extract/extractor as a noun.
Reader or reading active participle; also the regular Form III imperative قَارِئْ from قارأ, inferred from the dictionary lemma. Bare ء represents the hamza radical.
Reading, a verbal noun. Terminal ة may remain part of its lexical stem or be represented as a derivational ending; it is not a separate feminine agreement suffix here.
Believer/believing مُؤْمِن, insurer/assuring مُؤَمِّن, insured/secured مُؤَمَّن; also the conventional Arabic personal name Muʾmin. All retain root ءمن.
Responsible, questioned, or an official/person responsible. Hamza radical is canonical bare ء, irrespective of its written seat.
سَائِل is asker/beggar from سءل or fluid/flowing from سيل. Verb accepts the Form III imperative سَائِلْ from ساءل; the perfect سَاءَلَ has different spelling.
Usually principles, broken plural of مبدأ. Also a possible Form III active participle مُبَادِئ from بادأ, initiating/engaging another first. The latter noun/adjective reading is less common.
Speaker/saying from قول; also one taking a midday rest from قيل. The latter is a dictionary-attested homograph.
Said/quoted مَقُول, or nominal quoted matter; unmarked shadda also allows مُقَوِّل/مُقَوَّل participial readings, with the same root.
Balance/scale; the initial root و surfaces as ي in the instrument-noun pattern.
Appointed time/place or appointment; initial root و surfaces as ي.
Indefinite defective active participle دَاعٍ, caller/cause; final radical و has no separate surface span. Also the regular imperative دَاعِ from dictionary-attested داعى, inferred by conjugation.
Supplication/calling; also the conventional Arabic personal name Duʿāʾ. Surface final hamza is not a hamza radical.

رَامٍ is a thrower/archer from رمي; رَامَ sought/desired is from روم; رَامَ departed or a wound healed is from ريم. The last is less common and dictionary-attested. Imperative رَامِ from رامى also has root رمي.
Thrown/cast, مَرْمِيّ; can denote a thrown object. The final ي represents stem/root allomorphy and is not stripped as a pronoun.
Teacher/teaching مُدَرِّس or taught مُدَرَّس; also a possible place-of-study noun. The prefix belongs to the derived stem.
Stretched/extended; also a substantive grammatical category such as an extended noun. Geminate radicals are expanded in the canonical root.
Strong/severe/intense; root has repeated د radicals.
Readiness/preparation, verbal noun of استعدّ. The geminate root is عدد.
Earthquake/shaking, quadriliteral verbal noun.
Rolling/rolled, active or passive quadriliteral participle; substantival use is possible.
Rolling, quadriliteral verbal noun. Final ة is lexical/derivational, not a required gender-agreement morpheme.

Tranquillity. Uses the synchronic quadriliteral root listed by the Cairo Academy, with bare hamza; historical metathesis theories are not separate accepted roots. Terminal ة may be lexical or derivational.
Sparrows/birds, broken plural of عصفور. The Cairo Academy places this family under quadriliteral عصفر; the stem contains the broken-plural pattern.
Men, or men on foot/pedestrians as the broken plural of راجل. Adjectival pedestrian/on-foot use is also credible.
Usually houses, broken plural بُيُوت. Dictionary-attested بَيُّوت also describes something kept overnight or an affair that keeps one awake.
Mosques/places of prostration; broken plural, without a separable plural suffix.
Keys, broken plural of مفتاح; all surface letters belong to the stem.
Books كُتُب, or Form I/II active/passive verbal readings such as كَتَبَ، كُتِبَ، كَتَّبَ، كُتِّبَ، كَتِّبْ. No one vocalization is selected.

Knowledge عِلْم, flag/landmark عَلَم, knowing/teaching verbs with omitted vowels or shadda. Adjective additionally accepts the uncommon plural عُلْم of أعلم (cleft upper lip), explicitly listed in the dictionary.
Gold ذَهَب, or went/gilded and corresponding passive/imperative Form II readings. No vocalization is fixed.

Whole-word وَعْد promise or وَعَدَ promised; Waʿd is also a conventional personal name. و + عُدْ means and return (عود); و + عُدَّ/عَدَّ/عَدّ means and count/counted/counting (عدد); و + عِدْ is and promise (وعد).
قالَ said (قول) or took a midday rest (قيل). The dictionary also lists قال as a nominal word for speech and an adjective meaning speaking (قول).
Sold/bought (بيع), but also arm-span or stretching/striding/measuring by arm-spans (بوع), all dictionary-attested.
Threw/cast رَمَى; absent shadda may also allow an intensive Form II reading. Final ى is part of the weak stem.

دَعَا called/prayed has root دعو. دَعًّا pushing is an accusative verbal noun from دعع; دَعَّا can be its dual perfect. دَعَا can also be the dual imperative leave! from ودع. Dual and accusative-support alif are separately spanned in those readings.

أَكَلَ/أُكِلَ and eating/food أَكْل/أُكُل have root ءكل; أَكَلَّ made weary has root كلل. Interrogative أَ + كُلّ all is grammatical and rootless here; interrogative أَ + كَلّ dull/burdensome is lexical كلل. These parses require context.
Asked سَأَلَ, with canonical bare hamza root. No implicit spelling correction to other seated-hamza forms.
Read قَرَأَ; a final hamza radical written on alef. It remains distinct from قارئ and قراءة at the surface.

Imperfect plural, with active/passive and Form I/II vocalization ambiguity. The agreement prefix remains inside stem يكتب; ون is an inflectional ending. An alternative groups و and indicative ن separately.
Second-person feminine singular imperfect; active/passive and Form I/II readings share the letters. ين may be one ending or ي agreement plus indicative ن.
Plural imperative write!. Stem اكتب includes the imperative support vowel/prefix; وا combines the plural marker and its silent orthographic alif.
To/for their school or female teacher; emphatic لَ can instead precede a nominal predicate. ت is the construct form of ة. School may retain it lexically; teacher uses feminine inflection.
And with/by their book, or their writers (كُتّاب). Intensive كَتّاب prolific writer permits adjectival use. هم is the possessive enclitic.

Then/so at the schools; مُدارِس can also be a Form III studying/studying-with participle under the article. ف may be classified as conjunction or as a consequence/answer particle, which the contract does not distinguish.
Our children; broken plural أطفال followed by possessive نا.
Their female teachers/teaching females مُعَلِّمات, or taught/marked females مُعَلَّمات. ات is feminine plural and هم possessive.
With/in the two cars, or two feminine traveling/mobile referents. ت is the ة allomorph before dual ين. A lexical سيارة stem can keep ت; an agreement analysis can split it or group تين.
And the female students/seekers, or feminine plural seeking participle. ال is the article; ات is feminine plural.
Hospitals مُسْتَشْفَيَات or females seeking recovery مُسْتَشْفِيَات. The written ي belongs to the weak stem, followed by feminine plural ات.
Libraries/bookshops مَكْتَبَات, or feminine plural writing-related participles with different vowels/shadda (e.g. مُكَتِّبات). ات is the plural ending.
Vowels fix and with their book. Every combining mark stays with its preceding letter; suffix span contains هِمْ.
Vocalization fixes the active Form II participle: teacher/teaching. Shadda and kasra stay on the ل inside the stem.
Vocalization fixes the passive Form II participle: taught/marked; substantive use for a taught/marked person or thing is possible.
The supplied vowels fix the active perfect wrote. Do not admit the passive reading merely because inference strips marks.
The supplied vowels fix the passive perfect was written. Do not admit the active reading merely because inference strips marks.
Vocalized Form X verbal noun seeking forgiveness. Attached marks are covered by the single stem span.
Conventionally the Arabic name Muḥammad; also lexical مُحَمَّد much-praised, adjectivally or substantivally. The proper name retains its transparent Arabic root.
Cairo, or the feminine definite conquering/overpowering participle. The article is segmentable even in the proper name; ة may stay in the lexical stem or be feminine inflection.
Borrowed biblical personal name; no invented Arabic triliteral or quadriliteral root.
Borrowed name Washington. Initial و belongs to the name; it is not a conjunction here.
Two books كِتَابَان, or dual of intensive كَتَّاب prolific writer. ان is a nominative dual ending, not a numeral lexical POS.
Female writers or feminine plural writing participle; ات is inflectional plural.

Negative/future subjunctive particle لَنْ has no root; لِنْ be gentle/soft is the regular imperative of لان from لين, inferred from the dictionary lemma. The standalone grammatical token must still use a stem span under schema.ts.

Usually preposition فِي, rootless. Also feminine imperative فِي fulfill! from وفى, inferred by conjugation; and genitive construct mouth فِي from فوه. فِيَّ my mouth has fused case/pronominal ي and can take the enclitic boundary. These infrequent lexical readings require context.

Usually demonstrative هٰذا, treated as one stem or attention particle ه + demonstrative ذا. Unvocalized هذًّا is an accusative verbal noun rapid recitation/cutting from هذذ; هذَّا can be a dual perfect. The rare noun is attested in Lisan al-Arab; the dual is inferred.
Plural relative pronoun. Initial ال is retained within the lexical relative-pronoun stem, not assumed to be a productive definite article.
Independent first-person plural pronoun; no lexical Arabic root assigned.

Usually independent I. Also contracted أَنَّا that we (particle plus fused pronoun), or أَنًّا groaning / أَنَّا they two groaned from أنّ. Whole-stem segmentation is retained for the contracted grammatical token because the schema has no shared/fused span; separate ا represents accusative support or dual ending for lexical readings. Contraction segmentation remains uncertain.
Future particle سَوْفَ is rootless. سَوَّفَ/سَوِّفْ procrastinated/procrastinate and passive سُوِّفَ are lexical سوف; سَوْف also occurs as a verbal noun of smelling/patience in the dictionary.

مِنْ from is preposition; مَنْ who/whoever is pronoun, both rootless. مَنّ favor/manna or مَنَّ bestowed has root منن. Rare imperative مِنْ lie! (مين) and مُنْ provide for! (مون) follow the attested hollow verbs مان; those forms are inferred rather than directly cited.
Invalid: Latin characters are outside arabic-v1.
Invalid: ASCII digits are outside arabic-v1.
Invalid: contains whitespace; inputs are single words and are not trimmed.
Invalid: leading combining mark has no preceding Arabic letter to attach to.
Invalid: emoji is outside arabic-v1; it also occupies two UTF-16 code units.
Invalid: 33 Arabic letters exceed the maximum of 32 normalized letters.

limitations: AI-authored blind annotations, not human gold. Only frozen words, docs/CONTRACT.md and packages/core/src/schema.ts were read locally. No model outputs, teacher analyses, generated training data, fixture labels or other annotator files were inspected.

Field-level accepted sets are independent. Their Cartesian product is not a set of valid complete analyses; notes explain which reading motivates an alternative. These sets are not claimed exhaustive.

Canonical roots expand geminate radicals, preserve weak radicals and use bare ء for all hamza radicals. Rootless grammatical words and borrowed proper names use null. Transparent Arabic personal/place names may retain Arabic roots.

POS refers to the lexical head, not an attached preposition/conjunction. Participles with credible substantive and attributive uses accept both noun and adjective. This taxonomy is not fully defined by the contract and needs human adjudication.

The contract fixes coverage and span names but does not define all linguistic boundaries. Stem spans retain derivational prefixes, imperfective prefixes, internal broken-plural material and weak-root allomorphs. Orthographic endings are not re-expanded.

Standalone particles, prepositions and pronouns receive a stem span because schema.ts requires at least one stem. Contracted/fused forms cannot always be uniquely segmented with nonoverlapping surface spans.

Productive number/gender endings and enclitics are separated. Where a lexical feminine/masdar ending may reasonably be part of a lemma or derivational suffix, alternatives are supplied. Grouped versus separately spanned agreement endings are accepted where stated.

Offsets are original-input UTF-16 code units. Combining marks remain attached to preceding letters. Supplied diacritics constrain linguistic readings even though the documented initial model does not learn vowel distinctions.

Ordinary standard/classical dictionary readings and recognizable conventional names are included; unrestricted conversion of any word into a surname, brand, acronym or nonce borrowed name is not enumerated. Dialectal readings and speculative productive clitic combinations are not exhaustive.

Sources are primary dictionary/grammar texts rather than analyzer predictions. Where a source attests a lemma but not a particular inflected form, notes explicitly identify the conjugational inference.

Pattern and feature labels are intentionally omitted. Confidence concerns this finite accepted-set judgment; high confidence does not certify exhaustive analysis coverage. أنا has a specifically unresolved fused-segmentation convention.
